newsitem.title: USA: Global balloon attempt still on course.
newsitem.headline: Global balloon attempt still on course.

text.p: American Steve Fossett sailed far out over the Atlantic Ocean on Wednesday in his bid to become the first to circle the globe in a balloon and his expedition headquarters said the flight remained uneventful.
At 7:30 a.m. EST (1230 GMT) he was about 295 nautical miles east-southeast of Bermuda -- "very close to where we expected him to be," a spokesman said.
During the night the flight was routine with only periodic position reports coming from the craft, he added.
A heater that had gone out early in the flight was repaired and the 52-year-old adventurer no longer had to rely on a backup unit for warmth in his unpressurized gondola.

Fossett's solo attempt to make the record flight was expected to carry him northeast toward Britain, southeast over Europe to Ukraine and then east over Russia, Kazakhstan and China. After crossing southern Japan he would bridge the Pacific northeast to Washington state and land somewhere east of St. Louis, where he began the trip late on Monday night.
The route was likely to vary depending on where the jet streams take the helium and hot air craft.
Internet users may follow the progress of his trip at http://www.luc.edu/solo. The site includes Fossett's latest transmissions from the balloon and offers a chance to ask him questions.
The balloon was to hold an altitude of from 18,000 to 24,000 feet (5,500 to 7,300 metres) -- lower than two rival attempts that failed in recent days -- and the trip could take as long as 18 days.

Fossett, a wealthy Colorado-based commodities broker, is paying for the trip himself, with scientific backup from Loyola University of Chicago where his expedition control centre is based. He made a similar attempt one year ago but crashed in Canada on the second day.

A balloon piloted by Bertrand Piccard and Wim Verstraeten went down in the Mediterranean on Sunday six hours after taking off from the Swiss Alps. Fumes from kerosene leaking into the cabin brought down the Swiss-Belgian team.

And British tycoon Richard Branson and two crew members brought their Virgin Global Challenger balloon down in Algeria last Wednesday less than 24 hours after taking off from Morocco. Their craft had suddenly lost lift and plunged.
Fossett holds a world distance record for a solo balloon flight set in 1995 when he flew from South Korea to Canada.
